properties.entry:
Downloads of every kind, all from the buttons of the theme, in the look chosen in the top bar. The files are a report of the countries of the world in the language of the page, made on the server when they are asked for, in seven formats: a text, CSV, JSON, a chart as SVG and as PNG, a PDF, and a ZIP archive of them all.

Via Ajax: an AjaxDownloadButton from ui-components downloads with Wicket's AjaxDownloadBehavior: the page stays as it is and hears how the download ended, which a notification tells. Each button downloads in another Location of the behavior: into the browser, as a blob, through a hidden iframe, in a new tab or in the same window. While the file comes the button is busy: a spinner takes the place of its icon and it ignores clicks. Choose the file, and how the server answers: at once, slowly, to see the buttons busy, or with an error, to see which locations can tell.

Links: links the browser follows without Ajax, drawn as buttons by a ButtonBehavior: Wicket's DownloadLink of a file written on the server and deleted once downloaded, a ResourceLink to a resource of the page, a resource mounted at a URL of its own, which can be shared, the same resource showing a PDF in a new tab, and a file of the web application with the download attribute.

After a form: the buttons of a form send it via Ajax and, once it is valid, download the report it describes, or open it in a new tab, each with a ButtonDownloadBehavior, which makes any button busy while its download runs. The errors of the form are notifications.
Each button downloads the file chosen in another way, the page staying as it is; a notification tells how the download ended.
Links the browser follows without Ajax, drawn as buttons.
The buttons send the form and, once it is valid, download the report it describes or open it in a new tab.
The browser asks for the file with a request of its own into a blob, then saves it. The best choice for today's browsers: it tells whether the file came or the server failed.
A hidden iframe asks for the file, which the browser saves. The page never unloads, so its WebSockets stay open; it tells whether the file came or an error showed in the frame.
A new tab opens the file, which the server sends inline for the browser to show: a PDF, an image, a text; a ZIP is saved. A failure closes the tab again.

The window itself goes to the file, which the server sends as an attachment, so the browser saves it and the page stays; the page hears unload, though, which closes its WebSockets. It tells when the file came, never a failure.
The button waits while the server fails: the error would take the place of the page.
Wicket's DownloadLink: the server writes the file into its temporary folder when the link is clicked, sends it and deletes it.
A ResourceLink to a resource of the page, which makes the file when the browser asks for it.
A resource the application mounts at a URL of its own, which can be bookmarked and shared:
The same resource sends the PDF inline when asked to, and the link opens it in a new tab, which shows it.
A file of the web application, the picture of this demo, which the download attribute of the link saves instead of showing.
